index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..f0f2d299808f063775dbba3aba56dd66e14825fb 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -371,12 +371,52 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
 
+    Words in all caps, such as acronyms, are kept as they are. If the string
+    has no lowercase letters at all, its words are capitalized as usual::
+
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
+
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    # All caps only mark an acronym next to lowercase letters; a string that
+    # is all in uppercase, like a shouted heading, is titleized as usual.
+    if any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        title = _restore_acronyms(word, title)
+    return title
+
+
+def _restore_acronyms(word: str, title: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Put the words that are in all caps in ``word`` back into ``title``, the
+    titleized form of ``word``, as they are written in ``word``.
+    """
+    # Split ``word`` into words the way :func:`underscore` does, keeping
+    # their case.
+    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    words = re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", word)
+    # The words of ``title`` are its odd parts. They are the same words in the
+    # same order, except for a trailing "_id" that :func:`humanize` drops.
+    parts = re.split(r"([^\W_]+)", title)
+    title_words = parts[1::2]
+    if len(words) == len(title_words) + 1 and words[-1].lower() == 'id':
+        words.pop()
+    if len(words) != len(title_words):
+        # Unicode case mapping split or merged words; keep the title as is.
+        return title
+    for index, (original, titled) in enumerate(zip(words, title_words)):
+        if original.isupper() and original.casefold() == titled.casefold():
+            parts[2 * index + 1] = original
+    return ''.join(parts)
